topics.flagship-ru-ua: A new projection based on leaked official data suggests more than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the Ukraine war (3 outlets). Four outlets report that two Libyan naval officers died of wounds from a Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship docked in Benghazi, and Libyan authorities vowed retaliation against Kyiv. Ukraine's General Staff says it struck a major Russian air base and damaged five planes. Poland reportedly wants a no-fly zone near the Ukrainian border after repeated Russian airspace incursions, and allies are divided over Kyiv's strikes on Russian ships in Libya. Russia accused Estonia of hostile actions 'on the verge of unleashing open war' over planned border crossing closures from Dec. 1. A Russian strike on Sloviansk reportedly left one dead and 10 injured.
topics.flagship-ir-il: An Israeli strike killed a Hamas official, his wife and children in Gaza, the second senior Hamas security official killed in 24 hours (6 outlets). Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia continued: a Saudi skyscraper was hit again, with 11 injured and the coalition calling it a 'terrorist attack', and the Houthis claimed an attack on the Ras Tanura refinery. Iranian FM Araghchi said Israel is trying to drag the US into another war after an Israeli minister alleged Iran is building chemical weapons. NBC reportedly says Trump administration officials have discussed targeted killings of Iranian leaders. A Yemeni military official reportedly said Iran's IRGC and Hezbollah are directing Houthi attacks near Bab el-Mandeb, and the Iran war is being blamed for higher UK energy bills.
topics.T15: The stories are mixed and mostly local. King tides and storms prompted evacuation alerts along coastal B.C., and waves tore off the end of the Pacifica, California pier. One outlet describes this year's El Niño as potentially the most intense on record. A magnitude 5.1 quake struck Antique in the Philippines, and the Pentagon is reportedly planning for blackouts lasting up to 90 days. The Iowa Army plant was due to detonate nearly five tons of unstable lead azide explosives on Wednesday, and rent aid has begun for 970 flood-displaced families in Nuwakot, Nepal. One piece is an Indian government-promotional article.
topics.T01: RSF drone attacks overnight reportedly killed 19 in Sudan and injured at least 20, in an escalating drone war. Houthi officials say a Saudi-led airstrike on a Hodeida telecom hub killed 17 workers, and a separate Saudi airstrike on a house in Lahj reportedly killed eight displaced people; both are single-source reports. Other items include Myanmar junta airstrike survivors facing medical costs, Russian aircraft triggering an air raid alert on South Korea's Ulleung Island, and reporting that new landmine use and production undermine the ban treaty.
topics.T02: Amnesty International called for a war crimes investigation into Ethiopian and allied militia shelling in Tigray, saying it verified 14 civilian deaths in four attacks. Somalia's famine risk in Baidoa has decreased, but millions still face severe hunger. The ICJ's genocide ruling against Myanmar over the Rohingya drew coverage, including on the dilemma it poses for China. Other items cover UK-funded medical aid in Gaza, Taliban restrictions limiting women's access to care in Afghanistan, and a report that landmine casualties hit their highest level since 2020 (6,929 in 2025).
topics.T03: Israel's Defense Minister Katz said Israel and the US hold intelligence on an alleged Iranian chemical weapons program and that a preemptive strike remains possible (single source). Iran's foreign minister says Israel is trying to deceive the US into another war. Separately, a joint non-proliferation statement addressed Ukraine's report that Russia used riot control agents as a method of warfare, and the US Army is proceeding with a planned detonation of chemical material in Iowa.
topics.T04: Meningitis epidemic alert was issued for Gaza after a steep rise in cases (4 outlets). The EU's DG ECHO daily map tracks an Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak affecting DRC, Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda. Uganda's aviation authority ran its first public health emergency preparedness exercise at Entebbe Airport, and Incheon Airport is receiving AI fever-screening cameras.
topics.T05: Coverage is scattered and mostly single-source. A graft probe into Shanghai party chief Chen Jining reportedly upends expectations about China's succession. Other items include analysis of Tunisian President Saied's authoritarian drift, a German government report on alleged abductions and torture of Gülen-linked people in Turkey, Bangladesh's government telling diplomats that 'Awami terrorists' are creating fear, and Chile's lower house backing a tribunal for Cuban leaders. Nothing indicates an imminent coup.
topics.T06: Reporting is thin and mostly non-acute. India's Supreme Court declined interim bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the 2020 Delhi riots conspiracy case. The European Parliament urged Czechia to revise its public media reform after mass protests, and one outlet analyzes how French unrest and fuel prices could shape the 2027 election. Bangladesh plans a July Uprising memorabilia exhibition.
topics.T08: Colombia's president called a major blackout a 'terrorist attack', amid a week of armed-group attacks marking 10 years of faltering peace (2 outlets). A Jordan court sentenced a man to death over a terrorist attack (4 outlets, no details given). Indian police arrested a man in Meerut for allegedly plotting a suicide attack on an Army camp. Other items cover the US push for a hemispheric mutual defence pact against 'narco-terrorism', which Brazil and Mexico have not backed, and the EU's envoy ruling out normalization with the Taliban.
topics.T10: The US Navy contracted Raytheon to advance the SLCM-N submarine-launched nuclear cruise missile (single source). The RAF reportedly plans anti-drone nets and hardened hangars at UK bases, and a Pentagon loan of up to $15 billion to a startup tied to Donald Trump Jr. is under consideration. A US lawmaker urged Europe not to 'backslide' on defense spending, Germany's 2027 budget faces coalition strain over defense and pensions, and a Brookings report says US defense is at its lowest share of the federal budget since WWII.
topics.T11: Cambodia hosted its largest Golden Dragon exercise yet with Chinese forces (3 outlets). India and Nepal began 'Abhyas Suryakiran', focused on disaster management and forest warfare (7 outlets), and India and Sri Lanka are conducting Mitra Shakti 2026. US and Bangladesh coast guard forces concluded Guardian Shark 01, and three Russian Pacific Fleet ships arrived in Yangon for a joint exercise.
topics.T12: Hackers reportedly breached an open-source intelligence analysis system at the CIA (3 outlets), and the Treasury Department disclosed unauthorized access to systems at its financial crimes bureau. A report links an IRGC unit, Shahid Kaveh, to hacks on European freezers and US industrial devices, and US authorities are investigating suspected cyberattacks on up to 50 commercial ships, with Iran and Russia under scrutiny. Other items include a Microsoft Outlook/365 outage that led to a 'Code Red', a California suit against OpenAI over alleged hacking of Hugging Face, and a ransomware leak from a California city.
topics.T13: The coverage is sparse and largely partisan commentary. One outlet reports a record 2,100+ migrant arrivals in a single day on Spain's El Hierro, and another reports Spanish investigators found a coordinated element in July's Ceuta swim crossings (0-source item). An AfD leader called for 2.6 million deportations from Germany.
topics.T14: The US Embassy in Jerusalem issued a security alert urging Americans to exercise heightened vigilance amid Iranian and Houthi threats, warning of possible flight cancellations (single source).
topics.T16: Democrats reportedly secured at least 259 House seats, the largest majority since 1990. Trump awarded Rudy Giuliani the Presidential Medal of Freedom (3 outlets). Likud petitioned a Jerusalem court to review election results, and Nigerian coverage focuses on fears of violence ahead of the 2027 election after six were killed in Delta. New Zealand coverage covers slow election counts and a record rate of byelections.

bluf: An Israeli strike killed a Hamas official, his wife and children in Gaza, the second senior Hamas security official killed in 24 hours (6 outlets), and a separate report cites seven Palestinians killed in attacks that violate the ceasefire. A new projection from leaked official data estimates more than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in Ukraine (3 outlets); the estimate is unverified. Two Libyan naval officers died of wounds from a Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship docked in Benghazi, and Libya's military vowed retaliation against Kyiv, while NATO allies are divided over such strikes. A Saudi skyscraper was hit again in an attack Saudi civil defence blamed on the Houthis, injuring 11, and the Houthis separately claimed an attack on the Ras Tanura refinery. Iran's foreign minister Araghchi said Israel is trying to drag the US into another war after an Israeli minister alleged Iran is building chemical weapons. Katz reportedly said a preemptive strike remains possible, though that is single-source. NBC reportedly says Trump administration officials have discussed targeted killings of Iranian leaders (2 outlets). Hackers reportedly breached a CIA open-source analysis system (3 outlets), and Treasury separately disclosed unauthorized access at its financial crimes bureau.
